q: There are many branches of chemistry or chemistry disciplines.
e: True. There are many branches of chemistry or chemistry disciplines. That is how this part of the lesson is stated.

q: The different branches focus on different aspects of matter.
e: True. The different branches focus on different aspects of matter. That is how this part of the lesson is stated.

q: The five main branches are considered to be Organic chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry, Analytical chemistry, and Biochemistry.
e: True. The five main branches are considered to be Organic chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry, Analytical chemistry, and Biochemistry. Analytical chemistry finds what is in a sample and how much is there.

q: The five main branches are considered to be Organic chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry, Analytical chemistry, and Geochemistry.
e: False. It is not true that the five main branches are considered to be Organic chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry, Analytical chemistry, and Geochemistry. The usual five branches are organic, inorganic, physical, analytical, and biochemistry.

q: Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, and Theoretical chemistry are other branches of chemistry.
e: True. Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, and Theoretical chemistry are other branches of chemistry. That is how this part of the lesson is stated.

q: Organic chemistry is the area of emphasis on most carbon-containing chemicals which are hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
e: True. Organic chemistry is the area of emphasis on most carbon-containing chemicals which are hydrocarbons and their derivatives. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, especially hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

q: Organic chemistry is the area of emphasis on most oxygen-containing chemicals which are carbohydrates and their derivatives.
e: False. It is not true that organic chemistry is the area of emphasis on most oxygen-containing chemicals which are carbohydrates and their derivatives. Organic chemistry centres on carbon compounds, especially hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

q: Examples of organic chemistry include pharmaceuticals and plastics.
e: True. Examples of organic chemistry include pharmaceuticals and plastics. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, especially hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

q: Inorganic chemistry is the area of emphasis on, in general, matter that does not deal with hydrocarbons.
e: True. Inorganic chemistry is the area of emphasis on, in general, matter that does not deal with hydrocarbons. Chemistry studies matter and the changes matter undergoes.

q: Inorganic chemistry is the area of emphasis on, in general, matter that deals exclusively with hydrocarbons.
e: False. It is not true that inorganic chemistry is the area of emphasis on, in general, matter that deals exclusively with hydrocarbons. Inorganic chemistry is not about hydrocarbons; that is organic chemistry.

q: Examples of inorganic chemistry include minerals, metals and non-metals, and semi-conductors.
e: True. Examples of inorganic chemistry include minerals, metals and non-metals, and semi-conductors. Inorganic chemistry studies the rest of the elements and their compounds, not just hydrocarbons.

q: Physical chemistry is the area of emphasis on the behaviour and changes of matter and the related energy changes.
e: True. Physical chemistry is the area of emphasis on the behaviour and changes of matter and the related energy changes. Chemistry studies matter and the changes matter undergoes.

q: Physical chemistry is the area of emphasis on the static and unchanging nature of matter without related energy changes.
e: False. It is not true that physical chemistry is the area of emphasis on the static and unchanging nature of matter without related energy changes. Physical chemistry studies change, energy, and the behaviour of matter, not a static picture.

q: Examples of physical chemistry include reaction rates and reaction mechanisms.
e: True. Examples of physical chemistry include reaction rates and reaction mechanisms. Physical chemistry looks at how matter and energy behave in chemical systems.

q: Analytical chemistry is the area of emphasis on components and compositions of substances.
e: True. Analytical chemistry is the area of emphasis on components and compositions of substances. Analytical chemistry finds what is in a sample and how much is there.

q: Analytical chemistry is the area of emphasis on the synthesis and creation of new substances.
e: False. It is not true that analytical chemistry is the area of emphasis on the synthesis and creation of new substances. Analytical chemistry measures composition; synthesis is not its main job.

q: Examples of analytical chemistry include food nutrients, quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA).
e: True. Examples of analytical chemistry include food nutrients, quality control (QC) and quality assurance (QA). Analytical chemistry finds what is in a sample and how much is there.

q: Biochemistry is the area of emphasis on matter and processes of living organisms.
e: True. Biochemistry is the area of emphasis on matter and processes of living organisms. Biochemistry is the chemistry of living organisms and their processes.

q: Biochemistry is the area of emphasis on matter and processes of non-living organisms.
e: False. It is not true that biochemistry is the area of emphasis on matter and processes of non-living organisms. Biochemistry is about living organisms, not non-living matter.

q: Examples of biochemistry include metabolism and fermentation.
e: True. Examples of biochemistry include metabolism and fermentation. Biochemistry is the chemistry of living organisms and their processes.
